2608.02113.title: MemArbiter: Decision-Time Memory Arbitration for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
2608.02113.paper_summary: Large language model (LLM) agents must retain and use cross-step information to act coherently in long-horizon tasks. Existing methods improve memory accessibility, yet action-relevant information may still fail to guide the current decision because it is poorly formed, organized, prioritized, or presented. We call this post-access failure the Memory-Action Gap. We propose MemArbiter, a function-aware memory arbitration framework that addresses the memory-management-induced component of this gap. MemArbiter decomposes interaction histories into atomic items, organizes them into five functional Memory Banks, and combines bank-level demand, item-level relevance, focal-ambient representations, and a temporal presentation gate to dynamically control memory salience. We evaluate MemArbiter on ALFWorld against Flat Retrieval and Flat Recency under unified per-step memory budgets. With an open-weight action-generation model, MemArbiter achieves success rates of 82.8% and 92.5% under 500- and 750-token budgets, outperforming the strongest baseline by 20.9 and 25.4 percentage points, respectively. It also improves post-failure recovery and reduces failed-action repetition and state-action recurrence. These results show that function-aware memory arbitration enables accessible information to guide actions more effectively.
2608.02113.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）代理必須保留並使用跨步驟資訊，以便在長期任務中一致地行動。現有的方法提高了記憶的可及性，但與行動相關的資訊仍可能因為組織不當、優先級不明或呈現不佳而無法指導當前決策。我們將這種後訪問失敗稱為記憶-行動差距。我們提出了 MemArbiter，一個功能感知的記憶仲裁框架，旨在解決由記憶管理引起的這一差距的組成部分。MemArbiter 將互動歷史分解為原子項目，將其組織成五個功能性記憶庫，並結合庫級需求、項目級相關性、焦點-環境表示和時間呈現閘動態控制記憶的顯著性。我們在 ALFWorld 上評估 MemArbiter，與 Flat Retrieval 和 Flat Recency 在統一的每步記憶預算下進行比較。在開放權重的行動生成模型下，MemArbiter 在 500 和 750 代幣預算下分別達到 82.8% 和 92.5% 的成功率，分別超過最強基線 20.9 和 25.4 個百分點。它還改善了後失敗恢復，並減少了失敗行動重複和狀態-行動重現。這些結果顯示，功能感知的記憶仲裁使可及資訊能更有效地指導行動。
